newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: No decision yet to split Malaysia's Tenaga - Anwar.
newsitem.headline: No decision yet to split Malaysia's Tenaga - Anwar.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday that it was premature to assume that core electricity operations of state-controlled power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd would be broken up.
"The Ministry of Finance Inc, which has a majority stake in the utility firm, has not made any decision on the restructuring," Anwar was quoted as saying by the national Bernama news agency.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, was reacting to comments made by a Tenaga executive on restructuring plans.

Tenaga's senior general manager for finance, Rohailan Mohamed, said on Wednesday that the previously-announced breakup plan has been delayed from its September 1 launch. The utility has been undergoing changes and heavy scrutiny following a massive power outage on August 3.

The plan to break up Tenaga's generation, transmission and distribution functions into three units would help the utility become more accountable to shareholders and to the government, Rohailan told reporters at a regional oil conference in Singapore on Wednesday.
Tenaga first revealed the proposed restructuring in October last year.
Rohailan said Tenaga also planned to form two other units, one to focus on domestic non-core activities and another to manage its overseas activities.
But Anwar said Tenaga needed to submit fresh recommendations on the plan after the recent change in its leadership.
Ahmad Tajudin Ali took over as Tenaga's chief executive after the 15-hour blackout over peninsular Malaysia last month.
Anwar also said Rohailan's comments on the restructuring at an oil conference were not made at the right forum, Bernama said.
Tenaga officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
